r: The ALTOS principle is simple to state: public money must be traceable in a full circle, from the moment it is collected to the moment it is reported, with a named officer answerable at every point. The emblem of ALTOS is a 360° ring for that reason. Accountability that covers 300 degrees leaves a gap, and money leaks through gaps.

ALTOS is software for any Philippine local treasury. It records official receipts, remittances and deposits, checks and cash advances, the monthly reports of accountable officers, and the targets and results of collection. One database serves a desktop application and a web application used across the office network.

The software is only the visible part. Behind every screen is a rule taken from law, from the LTOM, or from COA regulations. ALTOS as a principle is the set of ideas that decided what those screens should do and what they should refuse to do.
Every transaction in a local treasury belongs to one of three movements.

items: Money comes in through taxes, fees, charges and transfers. Each peso is acknowledged by an accountable form, usually an official receipt (OR), issued by a bonded collecting officer.
Money goes out by check, by authorized cash advance, or by electronic transfer. Each release rests on an appropriation, a certified obligation and supporting documents.

Every collection and every disbursement is summarized, reconciled and reported upward and outward: to the treasurer, the accountant, the local chief executive, COA, the Bureau of Local Government Finance (BLGF) and the public.

r: The three are not a line but a loop. Reports feed the next cycle of targets and budgets, which shape the next round of collections. A treasury that collects well but reports late breaks the loop as surely as one that reports well but collects poorly.
In the figure, each movement carries its own forms, and the ring at the center stands for the one rule that holds them together: a named officer answers at every step.

Accountability in public administration is usually described in directions. Upward to superiors and oversight bodies. Downward to citizens. Horizontally to peer offices and auditors. ALTOS adds a fourth direction: across time. A record must be as trustworthy five years from now, under a different treasurer, as it is today.
In practice 360° accountability rests on four commitments.

items: No collection without a receipt, no release without a voucher.
A named, bonded officer is answerable for each form in custody and each peso in hand.
Reports are due on fixed dates, and the system counts the days.
Once posted, a record can be corrected only by a visible, logged act, never silently changed.

blocks.text: 1.4 The five questions in the Philippine setting

r: Five questions recur throughout this book.

head: Question
The question in full
Example from ALTOS
rows: Why does the practice exist, and which law requires it?
The official receipt exists because Presidential Decree (PD) 1445 requires every collection to be acknowledged.

A Report of Collections and Deposits (RCD) lists every receipt issued and every deposit made.
When is it due, and what sets it in motion?
The Report of Accountability for Accountable Forms (RAAF) and its consolidated version (CRAAF) are due on or before the 5th of the following month.
Where does it happen (in which office, fund or account), and who answers for it there?

The OR number is always the next in the series, and receipts must be issued in date order.

blocks.text: 1.5 Why a principle and not only a manual

r: Manuals tell an officer what to do when the case is ordinary. Principles tell the officer what to do when the case is new. The Philippines has strong manuals. What is often missing is a shared account of why the manuals say what they say. Without that, procedures decay into rituals, and rituals are the first thing cut when an office is busy.
The rest of this book traces the ALTOS principle back to the people who built public administration as a discipline, and forward to the daily work of a Philippine local treasury.

title: The Classical Founders and the Treasury Office

r: The classical founders gave the treasury its skeleton: a neutral career service, written rules, standard methods, clear functions and a chain of command. Each idea below still governs how a Philippine local treasury works, whether or not its staff know the names behind them.

blocks.text: 2.1 Woodrow Wilson (1887): administration as a field of its own

r: Wilson’s essay “The Study of Administration” argued that running a constitution is harder than framing one. Administration, he wrote, should be studied as a business-like field of its own, distinct from the making of policy.

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: The local treasurer is appointed by the Secretary of Finance, and serves the LGU as a career professional under each administration. Assessment and collection follow the tax ordinance, applied the same way to every taxpayer. ALTOS applies the same rate table to every taxpayer.

blocks.text: 2.2 Frank Goodnow (1900): policy and its execution

r: In
i
Politics and Administration
, Goodnow separated the expression of the public will from its execution. The politics–administration dichotomy was later criticized, but it still describes a useful division of labor.

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: The Sanggunian enacts the revenue code and the budget. The treasurer executes them. A treasurer may advise on rates but may not invent a fee that no ordinance authorizes. In ALTOS every line of an official receipt must be charged to an income account on the office’s chart of accounts.
Weber described bureaucracy as authority grounded in rules rather than persons. Its marks are fixed jurisdictions, hierarchy, written files, trained officials, and impersonal treatment of clients.

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: Every Weberian mark has a treasury form. Jurisdiction is the assignment of a collecting officer to a market or barangay. Hierarchy runs from collector to liquidating officer to treasurer. The written file is the receipt, the RCD and the cash book. Impersonality means the same procedure for every taxpayer, from the largest business to the smallest farm. Weber’s insight that “the file” outlives the official is the root of the ALTOS commitment that every record has a seal.
Taylor’s
i
Principles of Scientific Management
sought the most efficient method for each task through measurement and standardization.

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: Standard forms, standard codes for income accounts, and standard steps for issuing a receipt are Taylorist. So is measuring the time from collection to deposit. The danger of Taylorism is treating staff as parts of a machine. ALTOS standardizes the record but leaves the officer free to judge the case, such as when to grant a discount the ordinance allows.

blocks.text: 2.5 Henri Fayol (1916): the functions of management

r: Fayol named five elements of administration: planning, organizing, commanding, coordinating and controlling. He also set out fourteen principles, among them unity of command, division of work and order.

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: Unity of command means each collecting officer answers to one liquidating officer. Division of work separates collection from disbursement. Fayol’s “order” (a place for everything and everything in its place) is the stock room of accountable forms, where each booklet has a serial range and a custodian.
In
i
Papers on the Science of Administration
, which he edited with Lyndall Urwick, Gulick summarized the executive’s work as POSDCORB: Planning, Organizing, Staffing, Directing, Co-ordinating, Reporting and Budgeting.

head: POSDCORB
The local treasurer’s version
rows: Setting annual collection targets by source and by month
Dividing the office into collection, disbursement and records units
Designating bonded collecting, liquidating and disbursing officers
Assigning collection areas and issuing office orders
Working with the assessor, accountant, budget officer and the Business Permits and Licensing Office (BPLO)
RCDs; RAAF and CRAAF; Report of Checks Issued (RCI), Report of Disbursements (RD) and Liquidation Report (LR); cash position; statements of receipts and expenditures
Certifying cash availability and estimating income for the budget

r: Two of Gulick’s seven letters, Reporting and Budgeting, are about money and records. The treasury is where POSDCORB is most concrete.

blocks.text: 2.7 Herbert Simon (1947): decisions under bounded rationality

r: Simon’s
i
Administrative Behavior

attacked the “proverbs” of classical theory, which often contradicted each other. He placed the decision at the center of administration and showed that people decide with limited information, time and attention. He called this bounded rationality.

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: A treasurer cannot read every receipt. The answer is not more effort but better design of information: exception reports, alerts and dashboards that show only what needs attention. When ALTOS tells a collector that a RAAF is two days from its deadline, it is applying Simon. It narrows attention to the decision that matters now.

blocks.text: 2.8 How the founders’ ideas reached the Philippines

r: Public administration came to the Philippines with the American civil service in the early 1900s. It became an academic discipline when the Institute of Public Administration was set up at the University of the Philippines in 1952, now the UP National College of Public Administration and Governance. Filipino scholars such as Raul P. de Guzman, Ledivina V. Cariño and Alex B. Brillantes Jr. later adapted these ideas to Philippine governance, local autonomy and development.
The classical founders gave the treasury order. The next chapter shows how later thinkers added values that order alone cannot supply: equity, participation, results and public value.

title: From Waldo to New Public Governance

r: After 1945 the discipline asked a harder question than “how do we run things efficiently?” It asked “efficient for whom, and toward what end?” Each answer below added a value that the modern treasury must now serve alongside order and efficiency.
In
i
The Administrative State
, Waldo showed that the classical “principles” carried an unstated theory of values and governance. Choices about efficiency are also choices about values. No administrator is merely a technician.

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: Deciding which delinquent taxpayers to pursue first, or how to schedule market collections, affects who bears the burden of government. The treasurer exercises discretion and must be able to defend it in public terms.

The first Minnowbrook Conference, convened by Waldo, gathered young scholars who argued that administration should pursue social equity, not only economy and efficiency. H. George Frederickson made social equity the “third pillar” of public administration.

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: Equity appears in the law itself: the Local Government Code requires that local taxation be equitable and based as far as practicable on ability to pay. In practice it means accessible payment points, clear receipts in plain language, and no informal “fixers.” A citizen in a distant barangay should face the same procedure and cost as one beside the town or city hall.

blocks.text: 3.3 Vincent and Elinor Ostrom: polycentric governance

r: Vincent Ostrom challenged the single-hierarchy model and argued for many overlapping centers of decision. Elinor Ostrom’s
i
Governing the Commons
(1990) showed that communities can manage shared resources through rules they make and monitor themselves. She received the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 2009.

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: A local government is one center among many: the barangays, the province, the national agencies and civil society. Local revenue such as market fees, fishery rentals and the barangay share of real property tax depends on rules that local actors accept as fair. Ostrom’s design principles (clear boundaries, monitoring, graduated sanctions, low-cost conflict resolution) read like a guide to good local revenue administration.

blocks.text: 3.4 Public choice and New Public Management

r: Public choice theory, associated with James Buchanan and Gordon Tullock, applied economic reasoning to government decisions, treating public officials, like everyone else, as people who respond to incentives. In the 1980s and 1990s this fed New Public Management (NPM). Christopher Hood’s 1991 article named its doctrines: hands-on professional management, explicit standards and measures of performance, emphasis on output controls, and private-sector styles of management. David Osborne and Ted Gaebler’s
i
Reinventing Government
(1992) popularized it as “steering rather than rowing.”

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: Collection targets, collection efficiency ratios, performance-based bonuses, and the citizen’s charter required by the Anti-Red Tape Act (Republic Act or RA 9485, amended by RA 11032) all carry the NPM mark. NPM’s weakness is that what gets measured gets managed, and what does not get measured is neglected. A treasurer who chases the target can neglect the receipt.

blocks.text: 3.5 New Public Service (2000): serving, not steering

r: Robert and Janet Denhardt answered NPM with the New Public Service. Citizens are not customers. Administrators serve the public interest, which is built through dialogue, not found by adding up individual preferences.

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: A taxpayer is a citizen who funds a shared project, not a customer buying a service. Treating taxpayers as citizens means explaining where the money goes: posting statements of receipts and expenditures, answering questions at the counter, and treating complaints as a form of participation.
Mark Moore’s
i
Creating Public Value

asked managers to think like entrepreneurs for the public. His strategic triangle links three tests: Is the goal valuable to the public? Is it legitimate and supported by those who authorize it? Is it operationally possible?

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: ALTOS was tested against Moore’s triangle. Its value is faster, cleaner records and timely reports. Its legitimacy rests on following the LTOM, COA rules and the Data Privacy Act. Its operational capacity is the hardest test: it has to run on one laptop and one office network, for a small staff.

blocks.text: 3.7 New Public Governance (2006) and digital-era governance

r: Stephen Osborne described New Public Governance as a plural state in which services are produced through networks of public, private and civic actors. Patrick Dunleavy and colleagues argued in 2006 that NPM was giving way to digital-era governance: reintegrating fragmented services, organizing them around citizens’ needs, and using digital change as the engine.

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: Electronic payments through banks and payment channels, data exchange with the BLGF, and online access to statements are network governance. Digital-era governance warns against digitizing a broken process. ALTOS was designed by first redrawing the paper flow, then automating it.

blocks.text: 3.8 Good governance in the Philippine setting

r: Philippine scholars and agencies translated these schools into the language of good governance: transparency, accountability, participation and predictability. The Full Disclosure Policy of the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) requires local governments to post budgets, financial statements and procurement data. The Seal of Good Local Governance, institutionalized by RA 11292 in 2019, rewards sound financial administration among its core areas.

head: School
Core value it added
Question it puts to the treasurer
rows: Is every peso handled by rule?
Who bears the burden, and is it fair?
Do local actors accept the rules as theirs?
Did we reach the target at the least cost?
Did we explain ourselves to the people who pay?
Is it valuable, legitimate and doable?
Do our systems connect around the citizen?

r: The ALTOS principle borrows from every row. No single school is enough for a modern treasury.

title: Public Finance Theory for the Local Treasurer

r: Public fiscal administration sits where public administration meets public finance. The administrator asks how money should be handled. The economist asks how much should be raised, from whom, and for what. A local treasurer needs both.

blocks.text: 4.1 Adam Smith (1776): four canons of taxation

r: In
i
The Wealth of Nations

, Smith set four maxims for a good tax: equality (in proportion to ability), certainty (the amount and time are clear, not arbitrary), convenience (collected at a time and in a manner convenient to the payer), and economy (the cost of collection is small compared with the yield).

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: These canons are still the best test of a collection system. Certainty means a printed tax bill and a receipt that shows the legal basis of every charge. Convenience means payment windows, barangay collection days and e-payment. Economy means the cost of collecting a fee must not exceed the fee. ALTOS computes real property tax from the assessed value and the ordinance rate, so the taxpayer and the collector see the same figure.

blocks.text: 4.2 Richard Musgrave (1959): three functions of government finance

r: Musgrave’s
i
The Theory of Public Finance
divided the fiscal role of government into three branches: allocation (providing public goods), distribution (adjusting the distribution of income), and stabilization (smoothing the economy).

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: Local governments do mostly allocation: roads, health centers, markets, waste collection. Distribution and stabilization belong mainly to the national government. This is why the National Tax Allotment exists. It moves money from where it is raised to where services are needed.

Charles Tiebout (1956) argued that people “vote with their feet” among local governments offering different mixes of taxes and services. Wallace Oates (1972) stated the decentralization theorem: a public good should be provided by the lowest level of government that covers the area of its benefits.

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: The Local Government Code of 1991 put this theory into Philippine law by devolving health, agriculture, social welfare and other services to local governments. Devolution created a lasting gap between what local governments must spend and what they can raise themselves. Economists at the Philippine Institute for Development Studies, notably Rosario G. Manasan, documented this vertical fiscal imbalance and the heavy dependence of many local governments on national transfers.

blocks.text: 4.4 V. O. Key (1940): the missing budgetary theory

r: Key’s short article “The Lack of a Budgetary Theory” asked the question no one had answered: on what basis should money go to activity A instead of activity B? It remains the central question of every budget hearing.

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: The treasurer does not decide allocations, but the treasurer’s income estimates set the ceiling for every allocation. An honest, evidence-based estimate of local revenue is the treasurer’s contribution to Key’s question. Chapter 12 returns to this.
In
i
The Politics of the Budgetary Process
, Wildavsky showed that budgets are made by small adjustments to last year’s base, through negotiation among “guardians” and “advocates.” Budgeting is public policy expressed in numbers.

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: The treasurer is a guardian. Guardians earn trust by being right about the cash. A treasurer whose estimates are consistently realistic gains a voice in budget talks. One whose estimates prove unrealistic loses it.

blocks.text: 4.6 Principal–agent theory: why accountability needs information

r: Principal–agent theory, developed in economics by Michael Jensen, William Meckling and others, describes any relation in which one party (the principal) relies on another (the agent) who knows more and may have different interests. Contracts, monitoring and incentives reduce the gap.

blocks.label: IN THE TREASURY
r: The chain of principals and agents is long: citizens elect the Sanggunian and mayor, who rely on the treasurer, who relies on collecting officers. At each link the agent knows more than the principal. Accountable forms, fidelity bonds, reports with deadlines and audit trails are tools for closing the information gap. This is the economic logic behind 360° accountability.

head: Theorist
Idea
ALTOS application
rows: Computed tax bills; multiple payment channels
Funds and accounts tied to services
Decentralization to the lowest effective level
Barangay shares and local revenue codes
The treasurer as a credible guardian
Forms, bonds, deadlines and audit trails

r: A Philippine local treasury works inside a layered fiscal state: the Constitution grants local fiscal autonomy, the Local Government Code of 1991 gives it form, and national agencies supervise it. Since the Mandanas-Garcia ruling, local governments receive a larger share of national taxes and carry heavier responsibilities.
Article X of the 1987 Constitution guarantees local autonomy. Three of its provisions are the fiscal core.

items: each local government may create its own sources of revenue and levy taxes, fees and charges, subject to guidelines set by Congress.
local governments have a just share in national taxes, automatically released to them.
they are entitled to an equitable share in the proceeds of the use of national wealth within their areas.

r: Article IX-D creates the Commission on Audit (COA) with power to examine and audit all government revenues and expenditures. Local fiscal autonomy is therefore autonomy with audit, never autonomy from it.
Book II of the Code governs local taxation and fiscal matters. The provisions a treasurer meets daily include:

head: Provision
What it says, in brief
rows: Fundamental principles of local taxation: uniform, equitable, based on ability to pay, for public purposes, not unjust or confiscatory, and collected by the local government, never by a private person
Fundamental principles of local fiscal administration, beginning with: no money shall be paid out of the local treasury except under an appropriations ordinance or law
Each local government shall appropriate at least 20% of its annual internal revenue allotment, now the National Tax Allotment, for development projects
Real property taxation: assessment, rates, the Special Education Fund (SEF) levy, payment and remedies
The treasurer is appointed by the Secretary of Finance and is under the administrative supervision of the local chief executive, to whom the treasurer reports on tax collection efforts

r: Section 305 is the legal root of the ALTOS principle. Its rules (public money is held in trust, spent only for public purposes, properly documented and accounted for) are the 360° ring in statutory form.

blocks.text: 5.3 From IRA to NTA: the Mandanas-Garcia ruling

r: For nearly three decades the local share was called the Internal Revenue Allotment (IRA), computed from national internal revenue taxes collected by the Bureau of Internal Revenue (BIR). In the consolidated cases
i
Mandanas v. Ochoa
and
i
Garcia v. Ochoa

, G.R. Nos. 199802 and 208488, decided on July 3, 2018, the Supreme Court held that the just share must be computed from all national taxes, including customs collections. The words “internal revenue” in Section 284 were struck down as unconstitutional.

Since fiscal year 2022 the share has been released as the National Tax Allotment (NTA). To match the larger share with larger duties, Executive Order (EO) No. 138 (June 1, 2021) ordered the full devolution of certain national functions to local governments and created a Committee on Devolution. Executive Order No. 103 (November 6, 2025) extended the transition period.

blocks.label: WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE TREASURER
r: A larger NTA raises the 20% Development Fund in pesos, and with it the scrutiny of how that fund is used. It can also deepen reliance on transfers. The ALTOS view is that a bigger allotment makes local revenue effort more important, not less: own-source revenue is the measure of a local government’s fiscal citizenship.

The Automatic Income Classification of Local Government Units Act, signed October 26, 2023, sorts provinces, cities and municipalities into five income classes based on average annual regular income over three fiscal years, with a general reclassification every three years. Classification affects salaries, borrowing capacity and eligibility for programs. Accurate treasury records are therefore not only an audit matter. They decide the local government’s class.

head: Agency
Role toward the local treasury
rows: Department of Finance –Bureau of Local Government Finance (DOF-BLGF)

Supervises local treasury and assessment operations; processes the appointment of treasurers by the Secretary of Finance; issues the Local Treasury Operations Manual and policy on local revenue; collects fiscal data from local governments
Issues budget rules for local governments; releases the NTA; sets personal services limits
Audits all accounts; prescribes accounting rules and forms; issues audit observations and notices of disallowance
Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG)
General supervision of local governments; Full Disclosure Policy; Seal of Good Local Governance
Manages the national treasury; source of national standards on cash and banking
Reviews municipal tax ordinances and annual budgets

blocks.text: 5.6 Five questions for the fiscal state

items: is the treasurer appointed by the Secretary of Finance rather than by the mayor? To keep revenue administration professional and uniform across local governments, a Goodnow idea written into Section 470. The mayor supervises the treasurer and the DOF appoints and sets technical standards, so the two work together.
is the treasurer’s first duty under the Code? To collect what the ordinances levy and to release nothing without an appropriation.
are shares and reports due? On schedules set by DBM, COA and BLGF, gathered in the compliance calendar of Chapter 9.
does the money sit? In the funds the Code and the budget create: General Fund, Special Education Fund, Trust Fund, and the 20% Development Fund within the budget.
is autonomy kept honest? Through audit, disclosure and records that any successor can read.

title: The Local Treasury as an Institution

r: The local treasury is the custodian of the local government’s money and the keeper of its fiscal memory. Its authority comes from the Local Government Code, its procedures from the Local Treasury Operations Manual, and its discipline from the Government Auditing Code and the fidelity bond.

Under Section 470 of the Local Government Code, the treasurer is appointed by the Secretary of Finance from a list of at least three nominees of the local chief executive. A local treasurer must hold a college degree, preferably in commerce, public administration or law, and have treasury or accounting experience. The Code places a Master in Public Administration graduate squarely within the intended profile of the office.
The treasurer’s duties under the Code include:

items: taking custody of and properly managing local funds;
taking charge of the disbursement of local funds;
collecting taxes, fees and charges, and inspecting establishments for compliance with tax ordinances;
advising the local chief executive and the Sanggunian on fiscal matters, including income estimates for the budget;
certifying the availability of cash for obligations.

r: The Local Treasury Operations Manual (LTOM), 2nd Edition, was issued under DOF Department Order No. 085-2019 dated December 3, 2019. It sets the organization and staffing of treasury offices and the step-by-step procedures for collection, deposit, disbursement and reporting, with standard forms in its annexes. ALTOS follows the LTOM forms by name: the RAAF is Annex 16 of Book II and the CRAAF is Annex 17.

The LTOM is to the treasury what Taylor’s instruction cards were to the factory. It writes down the one best way so that every office does it the same way, and so that a newly assigned treasurer can take over without starting from zero.
An accountable officer is any official or employee whose duties permit or require the custody of government funds, property or accountable forms. In a local treasury the main roles are:

head: Role
Holds
Answerable for
rows: Accountable forms (official receipts) and cash collected
Every receipt in custody, issued or unused, and every peso collected until deposited or remitted
Collections remitted by collectors; reports received from them
Consolidating collections and the CRAAF; checking each collector’s RCD
Cash advances for payroll or petty expenses
Liquidating each advance within the prescribed period
Overall custody of funds, checks and forms
The whole treasury, including the acts of subordinates where supervision failed

r: Presidential Decree No. 1445 (1978) is the backbone of accountability for public money. Among its rules:

items: every officer whose duties involve the possession or custody of government funds or property is accountable for them and liable for their safekeeping;
the head of the agency bears primary responsibility for all government funds and property under the agency, and those who handle them are directly accountable to the head;
every accountable officer must be properly bonded (Section 101);
no payment of a claim may be made without the required documents and certification.

r: Section 101 of PD 1445 requires accountable officers to be covered by a fidelity bond. Bonding is administered by the Bureau of the Treasury under the Revised Omnibus Regulations on fidelity bonding, Treasury Circular No. 02-2009, as later amended. The bond amount follows the size of the accountability, and bonds must be renewed before they lapse.

blocks.label: IN ALTOS
r: The system keeps each officer’s bond amount and expiry date and warns before a bond lapses. By default it warns 60 days ahead, and it compares each bond with the cash the officer actually handled, flagging any bond that is missing, expired or too low. A rule on paper became a daily alert in the software.

Weber’s point that the file outlives the official is the institutional heart of the treasury. Treasurers, mayors and collectors change. The obligations of the LGU and the rights of taxpayers do not. An institution is a set of rules and records strong enough that a stranger can take over tomorrow and continue without loss.

This is the test every treasury reform should face: will it still work after the person who started it has left? The question is personal for an acting treasurer on a final designation with a fixed end. Chapter 13 returns to it.

Collection is where the citizen meets the treasury, and where most leakage begins. The ALTOS rule for collection is that no peso enters the treasury without an accountable form, issued in sequence, by a bonded officer, and deposited intact.

blocks.text: 7.1 Why collection matters more than ever

r: Own-source revenue measures how far a local government funds itself. Even after the Mandanas-Garcia ruling, many local governments depend on the National Tax Allotment for most of their income. Every peso of local revenue widens the room for local choice. It also builds the habit of paying for local services that makes local democracy real.

head: Source

rows: In a province, the municipal treasurer collects it and the proceeds are shared among province, municipality and barangays

r: The Real Property Valuation and Assessment Reform Act (RA 12001), signed June 13, 2024, sets national valuation standards and requires a single Schedule of Market Values in each local government, prepared by the assessor, reviewed by the BLGF and certified by the Secretary of Finance. Many local governments are now preparing revised schedules, which will change the tax base the treasurer collects on.

Collection has seasons. January carries business permit renewals, the first quarter or full-year payment of real property tax with any prompt-payment discount the ordinance grants, and most community tax certificates. Real property tax installments fall due quarterly. Market and other charges are collected daily. A treasurer who plans staff and cash handling around this calendar applies Gulick’s Planning and Staffing to the most concrete task in government.

Money is collected at the treasury windows, at markets and terminals, in barangays on collection days, and through banks and payment channels. Each point needs a named collecting officer with forms in custody. The farther the collection point is from the office, the stronger the controls must be, because supervision is weaker.

blocks.text: 7.5 How: the life of an official receipt

items: Forms are received from the supplier and recorded in the stock of accountable forms, by serial number.
A booklet or series is assigned to a named collecting officer and recorded against that officer’s accountability.
The amount due is computed from the ordinance or the tax declaration, not negotiated.
The receipt is issued in serial order, in date order, with each charge on its proper income account and fund.
Collections are deposited intact, usually the same or next banking day, and listed in the Report of Collections and Deposits (RCD).
Used, unused and cancelled forms are reported monthly in the RAAF.

blocks.label: IN ALTOS
r: The software enforces steps 4 and 5. The next OR number is always the next in the series. A receipt cannot be dated before the series was issued or before the last receipt. Once an RCD is prepared for a date, no receipt can be added on or before that date for the same officer and account. When one receipt carries charges for two funds, such as basic real property tax and the SEF, ALTOS records one portion per fund so each fund’s RCD and bank account receive their own share.

A spoiled receipt is never destroyed. It is marked cancelled, kept with all copies, and reported. A correction is a new, visible act with a stated reason, never an erasure. This is one of the oldest internal controls in public finance, and ALTOS preserves it: a cancelled OR stays in the series with its status and the reason, the cancellation is written to the audit log under the user’s name, and an OR already included in an RCD can no longer be cancelled.

Collection is also where public administration’s later values meet the classical ones. Smith’s convenience and Frederickson’s equity both ask the treasury to go to the taxpayer: barangay collection days, clear bills, payment by bank or e-wallet. EO 170 enjoins local governments to offer digital payment while keeping cash and traditional methods available. Convenience for the citizen must never come at the cost of the receipt.

Disbursement is where public money becomes public service, and where the law is strictest. The ALTOS rule for disbursement is that every peso released rests on four things: an appropriation, an obligation, cash actually available, and a named payee who signs for it.

blocks.text: 8.1 Why disbursement is guarded more than collection

r: Collection errors usually lose money the government never had. Disbursement errors lose money the government already holds in trust. Section 305 of the Local Government Code therefore opens with a prohibition: no money shall be paid out of the local treasury except under an appropriations ordinance or law. Section 344 adds that no money may be disbursed unless the budget officer certifies the appropriation, the accountant has obligated it, and the treasurer certifies that funds are available.

head: Officer
Certifies
Question answered
rows: An appropriation exists for the purpose
Did the Sanggunian authorize this kind of spending?
The appropriation has been obligated; supporting documents are complete
Is this a valid claim against that appropriation?
Cash is available in the fund
Does the head of the local government accept responsibility?

r: This is segregation of duties in its classic form (Chapter 10). No single officer can both authorize and release money.

blocks.text: 8.3 What comes before the check: procurement

r: Most large disbursements follow a procurement. The New Government Procurement Act (RA 12009), signed July 20, 2024 and in effect since August 13, 2024, replaced RA 9184 and introduced new award criteria such as the Most Economically Advantageous and Responsive Bid. Its implementing rules were published on February 10, 2025. The treasurer does not run procurement, but cannot pay a contract that skipped it.

items: Checks are drawn on the fund’s bank account from a check booklet in the custody of a disbursing officer, in serial and date order, against an approved disbursement voucher. Checks issued are listed in the Report of Checks Issued (RCI).

A disbursing officer receives a cash advance for a specific purpose, such as payroll or petty expenses, under COA rules on cash advances. The officer reports payments in the Report of Disbursements (RD) and settles the advance through a Liquidation Report (LR), returning any balance.
EO 170 (2022) allows payments directly into the bank or e-money accounts of payees, with the same documents behind them.

blocks.label: IN ALTOS
r: Check booklets are recorded by bank account and serial range, and number ranges may not overlap. Checks must be prepared in chronological order and cannot be dated before the booklet was assigned. Each check shows its disbursement voucher, whether it has been released and to whom, and whether it is already in an RCI. Cash advances are tracked until liquidated.

Section 287 of the Local Government Code requires each local government to appropriate at least 20% of its annual internal revenue allotment, now the National Tax Allotment, for development projects. The main guidelines are in DBM-DOF-DILG Joint Memorandum Circular No. 1 dated November 4, 2020, supplemented by later circulars such as Joint Memorandum Circular No. 01 dated April 27, 2023. Readers should confirm the circulars in force before relying on them.
The 20% Development Fund (20% DF) is the clearest test of whether a larger NTA becomes development or disappears into operations. Because the NTA rose after Mandanas-Garcia, the fund rose with it.

blocks.label: IN ALTOS
r: The 20% Development Fund (code 100-DF) and its account, Share from National Tax Allotment – 20% Development Fund, are built into every database. They cannot be renamed, deactivated or separated, so the fund is always visible in collections, disbursements and reports.

items: public money is held in trust; spending it without authority is a breach of that trust and a ground for disallowance by COA.
an appropriation, an obligation, cash, an approved voucher and the payee’s acknowledgment.

from the fund that holds the appropriation, through that fund’s bank account.

r: Reporting closes the 360° ring: a peso is fully accounted for only when it appears, correctly, in a report someone else can check. The ALTOS rule for reporting is that every report has a form, an owner, a deadline and a reader, and that the system counts the days.

A record proves that something happened. A report proves that someone answered for it. Gulick put Reporting in POSDCORB because an executive who does not report cannot be held to account, and Simon showed that a decision-maker sees only what the information system shows. In a treasury, the report is the moment when private knowledge of the officer becomes public knowledge of the institution.

blocks.text: 9.3 When: the deadline as a management tool

r: Deadlines are not paperwork. They limit how long an error or a shortage can stay hidden. A shortage found on the 5th of the next month is at most five weeks old. A shortage found at the year-end audit can be thirteen months old.

blocks.label: IN ALTOS
r: RAAF and CRAAF deadlines are computed for each month. On each officer’s home page, ALTOS shows how many days are left, “due today,” or how many days overdue. The liquidating officer sees which RAAFs have not yet been received. Each submission is recorded with its date, and a late one is flagged with the number of days late. Only the System Administrator can cancel a submission recorded by mistake, and must state the reason.

ALTOS gathers the treasury’s recurring deadlines into one compliance calendar. Some items come from the system’s own records and clear themselves once done. Others are standing deadlines the System Administrator can edit.

items: RAAF and CRAAF for each officer and month; fidelity bonds expiring or missing; ORs not yet included in an RCD; cash advances not yet liquidated.

the last day to pay the quarter’s real property tax without interest; posting the notice of delinquency; business permit renewal and quarterly business tax installments; the SRE to the BLGF; the monthly bank reconciliation.

r: The defaults name their legal basis and, where a deadline depends on a current circular, tell the user to verify it. A calendar that admits its own uncertainty is safer than one that pretends to know.

Reports flow not only upward to COA, BLGF and DBM, but outward to citizens. The DILG’s Full Disclosure Policy requires local governments to post key financial documents, including the annual budget, statements of receipts and expenditures, and procurement information, in conspicuous places and online. This is the New Public Service in practice: citizens who pay are told what was collected and how it was spent.

items: to turn private custody into public accountability, upward, outward and across time.

title: Segregation of Duties and the Architecture of Trust

r: No single person should be able to start, approve, record and conceal a transaction. Segregation of duties is the oldest internal control in public finance, and it is Weber’s bureaucracy turned into a safeguard: authority split among offices so that each checks the next.

blocks.text: 10.1 Why trust must be designed, not assumed

r: The principal–agent problem of Chapter 4 does not assume that officers are dishonest. It assumes only that they know things their principals do not. Good people make errors, and errors that one person can both make and hide grow into losses. A well-designed office protects honest staff as much as it deters dishonest ones: when every step has a second pair of eyes, no one carries suspicion alone.

The international reference is the Internal Control – Integrated Framework of the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission (COSO), adopted for the public sector by the International Organization of Supreme Audit Institutions (INTOSAI). In the Philippines, the DBM’s National Guidelines on Internal Control Systems apply the same ideas to government. All describe five components.

head: Component
Meaning
Treasury example
rows: Tone at the top, integrity, competence
A treasurer who follows the same rules as everyone else
Remote collection points, cash advances, unreconciled accounts
Four signatures on a voucher; monthly bank reconciliation
Reliable, timely records reaching the right people
Surprise cash counts; COA audit; review of exception reports

items: The person who holds the cash should not be the only one who records it.
Money coming in should not be used to pay money going out without passing through the bank and the books.
The officer who approves a payment is not the one who hands over the check.
The officer who made an entry should not be able to change it quietly afterward.

r: ALTOS gives each user one of four roles, and each role sees only the pages its duties require.

head: Role
Can do
Cannot do
rows: Issue ORs from assigned series, prepare own RCD, prepare and submit own RAAF
Change a posted receipt or RCD; act for another officer

r: The most important rule in ALTOS is short:
b
only the System Administrator changes data already encoded.

An officer who finds an error asks for a correction through Sysadmin › Data Correction, and the correction, its reason and its author are written to the sealed audit log. When the System Administrator opens another user’s page to help, every action there is logged as done by the administrator acting for that user.

A local treasury may have only a handful of staff. Perfect segregation is not always possible. When one person must hold two roles, compensating controls take over: more frequent review by the treasurer, surprise cash counts, monthly reconciliation by someone outside the cash function, and exception reports that show unusual patterns. ALTOS supplies the exception reports. The treasurer must supply the review.

The sharpest test of segregation is whether it binds the person at the top. In ALTOS the System Administrator, often the treasurer, has the widest powers, and so is the one most completely logged. The audit trail exists first for the person who could most easily do without it. That is the architecture of trust: power and visibility grow together.

title: The Sealed Ledger: Integrity, Security and Data Privacy

r: A digital ledger is only as trustworthy as the proof that no one has quietly changed it. The ALTOS answer is the sealed ledger: records that can be corrected only in the open, an activity log that reveals any deletion or alteration, and personal data protected as the law requires.

blocks.text: 11.1 Why paper had integrity and screens do not

r: A bound cash book with numbered pages carries its own proof: a torn page or an erasure shows. A database has no pages. Anyone with enough access can change a number and leave no mark. Digital transformation therefore removes an old safeguard and must replace it with a new one. Without a seal, an electronic record is weaker evidence than the paper it replaced.

items: Taxpayer names, addresses, property holdings and payments are personal information. The LGU is a personal information controller and must protect them with organizational, physical and technical measures. The National Privacy Commission (NPC) requires notice of certain personal data breaches within 72 hours of discovery.
Unauthorized access to, or interference with, a government system is a crime.
Accounting records and supporting documents must be preserved and made available to the auditor.
Electronic documents may be admitted as evidence if their integrity can be shown.

r: The Cybersecurity Framework of the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) groups security work into functions. Version 1.1 named five: Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond and Recover. Version 2.0 (2024) added a sixth, Govern, placing security under the organization’s leadership and risk strategy. The Google Cybersecurity Professional Certificate, which I completed in 2025, teaches the framework as a working tool. ALTOS organizes its Security Center by the five original functions; governance rests with the treasurer as System Administrator.

head: Function
What ALTOS does
rows: A self-assessment of every safeguard below, with its current status

Passwords stored only as one-way hashes (PBKDF2-SHA256, 200,000 iterations), so no one, not even the administrator, can read them; password policy with expiry and no reuse; lock-out after repeated wrong passwords; automatic log-out after 15 minutes idle, for every user including the administrator; encrypted backups (AES-256)
A tamper-evident activity log; security events such as failed log-ins, log-ins outside office hours, password resets, data corrections and setting changes; an integrity check of the program files
An incident register with playbooks, including the 72-hour notice to the National Privacy Commission for personal data breaches
Encrypted backups with a recovery key kept on paper by the System Administrator; a restore drill that decrypts and checks the latest backup

r: Every entry in the ALTOS activity log carries a cryptographic code (an HMAC-SHA256) computed from the entry itself and from the code of the entry before it. The secret key is kept outside the database. If anyone deletes or changes an entry, every code after it stops matching, and the integrity check reports where the chain breaks.
This is Weber’s written file in digital form. The file does not depend on the honesty of whoever holds it today, because any tampering is visible to whoever reads it tomorrow.

A sealed ledger is not a frozen one. Errors happen and must be corrected. The rule is that the correction is a new event, with a reason and an author, not a silent overwrite. In ALTOS, posted receipts, RCDs and reports are corrected only by the System Administrator through Data Correction, and each correction enters the sealed log.

blocks.text: 11.6 Lessons for any local government going digital

items: Keep passwords, encryption keys and backups out of shared folders and program copies.
Encrypt every connection that carries taxpayer data across a network before going live.
Test a restore, not just a backup. A backup never restored is a hope, not a control.
Write down who may see what, and make the system enforce it.
Plan for the laptop that is lost, the server that fails and the staff member who leaves.

r: Security is not a feature added at the end. It is the digital form of the fidelity bond: a guarantee that the public’s money and the public’s records will be there tomorrow.

The records a treasury keeps for accountability are also its best evidence for management. The ALTOS position is that analytics should answer the treasurer’s real questions (Are we on target? Who has not paid? Where could money be leaking?) and that every result is a prompt for a human decision, never an automatic action.

Robert Behn argued in 2003 that public managers measure performance for eight different purposes: to evaluate, control, budget, motivate, promote, celebrate, learn and improve. Each purpose needs a different measure. A treasurer who uses one number, such as total collections, for all eight will misread the office. Collection efficiency tells you about improvement. RCD timeliness tells you about control. A target met tells you when to celebrate.

blocks.text: 12.2 From the classroom to the treasury: the data analysis process

r: The Google Data Analytics Professional Certificate, which I completed in 2026, teaches a six-phase process: Ask, Prepare, Process, Analyze, Share and Act. I found that each phase has a natural home in the treasury. The process turns a pile of receipts into an answer a treasurer can act on.

r: Two lessons from that training shaped ALTOS most. First, the language of the data matters: ALTOS keeps its records in an SQL database and is written in Python, the same tools those courses teach, so any analyst trained in them can read its data. Second, data ethics comes with data skills. ALTOS exports data for further analysis in Jupyter or Google Colab only in de-identified form, without names or addresses, in keeping with the Data Privacy Act.
This is where the book departs from most public administration texts. The founders told us to manage by facts. Modern analytics shows how, with tools a local treasury can afford.

Targets are the NPM contribution to the treasury (Chapter 3), and income estimates are the treasurer’s answer to V. O. Key’s question (Chapter 4). ALTOS keeps annual targets for eight revenue sources that follow the SRE grouping: Real Property Tax – Basic, Special Education Tax, Tax on Business, Other Taxes, Regulatory Fees, Service and User Charges, Receipts from Economic Enterprises, and Other Receipts. Collections are compared with targets by month and by source, and this year is compared with last year.

For real property tax (RPT), ALTOS defines collection efficiency as RPT collected this year divided by the sum of what was collected and what is still collectible, for property units whose payment history is recorded. Units without history are counted separately with their annual tax as an estimate, so the office sees how complete its picture is. A ratio that hides its own coverage invites false confidence.

A treasurer is asked in every budget season what the year will bring. ALTOS forecasts year-end collections from the seasonal pattern of up to three past years, or from a linear trend when there is not enough history. It reports an 80% range and the chance of reaching the target. A forecast with a range is honest about uncertainty. A single number pretends to know.

head: Insight
Method
Decision it supports
rows: Two-proportion z-test: owners who paid within 30 days after a notice against delinquent owners without one
Whether to invest staff time in sending notices
Logistic regression on past notice outcomes; a transparent rule-based estimate while history is thin
Which delinquent accounts to visit first
k-means clustering of property units by payment behavior
Statistical flags: cancelled ORs, RCD lag, Benford’s law on first digits, near-threshold and duplicate checks, unusual collection days
Where to look first in a surprise review
What to correct with the assessor
CSV files without names or addresses
Further analysis by students or analysts without exposing personal data

r: Benford’s law deserves a note. In many natural sets of financial figures, the leading digit 1 appears about 30% of the time and 9 under 5%. Invented figures rarely follow this pattern. Auditors use it as a screening tool, not as proof. ALTOS uses it the same way.

The statistical methods in this table are the ones taught in the Google Advanced Data Analytics Professional Certificate: hypothesis testing, regression and clustering. Here they are applied to a local treasury’s own records instead of a textbook dataset.

blocks.text: 12.7 Evidence and the Seal of Good Local Governance

r: The Seal of Good Local Governance, institutionalized by RA 11292 (2019), assesses local governments on core areas that include financial administration and sustainability. Indicators such as the growth of locally sourced revenue, compliance with full disclosure, and use of funds can be shown far more easily when the treasury’s records are complete and searchable.

Simon’s bounded rationality cuts both ways. Analytics narrows attention to what matters, but it also hides what is not measured. Campbell’s law warns that the more a quantitative indicator is used for social decision-making, the more it can distort the very work it was meant to measure. A treasurer who rewards collectors only on volume may get volume at the cost of the receipt. The safeguard is to pair every target with a control measure: collections with RCD timeliness, notices sent with complaints received.

title: Digital Transformation of the Local Treasury: Lessons from Building ALTOS

r: Digital transformation succeeds when the paper process is first understood, then redrawn, then automated, and when the result survives the people who built it. Building ALTOS alongside daily treasury work taught eight lessons that apply to any Philippine local government.

blocks.text: 13.1 Lesson one: start from the form, not the screen

r: Every ALTOS page began with an LTOM or COA form: the official receipt, the RCD, the RAAF, the check register, the liquidation report. The screen is a way of filling the form correctly. A system designed from screens drifts away from the law. A system designed from forms stays auditable.

blocks.text: 13.2 Lesson two: encode the rule, not just the record

r: The greatest value of software is not storage but enforcement. A rule written in a manual depends on memory. A rule written into the system applies on the busiest day. The next OR number is always the next in series. A check cannot predate its booklet. The 20% Development Fund cannot be deactivated. Each of these is a sentence of law turned into a constraint.

blocks.text: 13.3 Lesson three: one database, many doors

r: ALTOS serves a desktop application and a web application from one database. Staff on the office network use a browser; the administrator can use either. Every change is made in both so that the two never disagree. Two systems that each hold part of the truth are worse than one system that holds all of it.

blocks.text: 13.4 Lesson four: design for the people who are not the developer

r: The interface uses the words of the treasury, not of programmers. Buttons are named for the act (“Submit RAAF,” “Prepare / Print CRAAF”). Alerts say what to do and by when. The test of a public system is whether a collecting officer with no training in computers can use it correctly on the first day.

blocks.text: 13.5 Lesson five: continuity is a public obligation

r: When a treasury runs on one computer, that computer becomes a single point of failure. Closing a laptop can stop every collector in the office. A public system needs a continuity plan: where the system runs when the main machine is away, who can restore it, and how long the office can work on paper meanwhile. EO 170 itself requires the national agencies it covers to adopt a business continuity plan. The options include a reserve machine, the LGU’s own server run by its information technology office, or a documented fallback to manual forms with later encoding.

blocks.text: 13.6 Lesson six: turnover is part of the design

r: An acting treasurer’s designation has a fixed end. ALTOS therefore includes a turnover function that assembles the records, verifies them and produces a certificate for the incoming officer. The goal is Weber’s: the file outlives the official. A reform that leaves with its author was never an institution.

blocks.text: 13.7 Lesson seven: settle ownership and authorship early

r: Software written by a public official raises questions of ownership. The Intellectual Property Code (RA 8293) provides that no copyright subsists in a work of the Government, defined as a work created by an officer or employee as part of regularly prescribed official duties. For works made in the course of employment, copyright belongs to the employer only when the work results from regularly assigned duties, unless there is an agreement to the contrary.
Writing software is not among the statutory duties of a local treasurer, but the answer in a given case depends on the facts. A developer-official should:

items: keep a dated record of authorship (source files, design notes, versions);
register or deposit the work with the Intellectual Property Office of the Philippines (IPOPHL) where appropriate;
agree in writing, through a memorandum of agreement or license, how the local government may use, maintain and host the system after the developer leaves;
seek the advice of legal counsel before any commercial use.

r: Clear terms protect both sides. The LGU keeps a working system and its records. The developer keeps the authorship. Taxpayers keep continuity of service.

blocks.text: 13.8 Lesson eight: the practitioner can be the builder

r: Local governments usually face two choices for treasury software: buy a package that does not fit their rules, or wait for a national system. ALTOS shows a third path. A practitioner who knows the law and the forms, and who learns modern data and digital skills, can build a tool that fits the office exactly. Those skills are no longer locked in universities. I learned much of what ALTOS needed through seven Google Professional Certificates, hundreds of hours of online study taken alongside the daily work of the treasury: Cybersecurity, Project Management, Data Analytics, Advanced Data Analytics, Business Intelligence, AI and IT Support. Their marks are visible in the system: cybersecurity in the Security Center, and analytics and business intelligence in Data Analytics and its Insights. The courses supplied the method: how to frame a question, clean data, analyze it and present it. The treasury supplied the problems. The MPA supplied the reason: public value, accountability and the public interest.

The lesson for public administration education is direct. Future treasurers, budget officers and accountants should learn data skills as part of their professional formation, not as an optional extra. The best person to digitize a process is often the person who has carried it out by hand.

It is not buying computers. It is not scanning paper. It is not a website. Digital transformation in a treasury means that the rules of public finance are carried out, recorded and reported by a system that any authorized person can check, and that continues to work when the people change. Dunleavy’s digital-era governance (Chapter 3) and Weber’s bureaucracy (Chapter 2) meet here: integration through technology, discipline through records.

title: The ALTOS Framework: Ten Principles for Philippine Public Fiscal Administration

r: The ALTOS framework condenses this book into ten principles. Each joins a founder’s idea to a Philippine rule and a practice a treasury can adopt tomorrow, with or without software.

items: Every collection and every release must trace to a law, an ordinance or an appropriation.
Goodnow’s distinction between policy and administration; RA 7160 Secs. 130 and 305.
No collection without an accountable form, no release without a voucher.
A named, bonded officer answers for each form in custody and each peso in hand.
principal–agent theory; PD 1445 Sec. 101; Fayol’s unity of command.
Reports fall due on fixed dates, and the days remaining are visible to the officer and the supervisor.
Gulick’s Reporting; Simon’s bounded attention; the RAAF and CRAAF due on the 5th.
Posted records change only through a visible, reasoned, logged correction.
Weber; RA 8792 on electronic evidence; the NIST framework.
No one person both authorizes and releases, or both holds and records, public money.
Fayol’s division of work; the COSO framework; RA 7160 Sec. 344.
Each peso stays in the fund the law assigns it, including the Special Education Fund and the 20% Development Fund.
Assess fairly, collect conveniently and disclose fully.
Adam Smith’s canons; Frederickson’s social equity; the Denhardts’ New Public Service; the Full Disclosure Policy.
Targets, forecasts and control checks inform the treasurer’s judgment but never replace it.
V. O. Key; Simon; Behn; Moore’s public value; the Ask–Prepare–Process–Analyze–Share–Act process of data analytics (Chapter 12).
Records, rules and systems must work after the incumbent leaves, with clear turnover, continuity plans and settled ownership.
Weber’s institution; Ostrom’s durable rules; digital-era governance.

r: The principles can serve as a self-assessment. A treasurer can rate the office on each principle from 1 (absent) to 4 (practiced and evidenced), identify the two weakest, and act on those first. They can also serve as a teaching outline for public fiscal administration courses, pairing each principle with its founding thinker and its Philippine law.

blocks.label: IN ALTOS
r: The self-assessment is built into the system as Sysadmin › Analytics › ALTOS Framework, on the desktop and on the web. For each principle the system first shows what its own records say. Examples: fee items without a Revenue Code section, checks without a voucher number, officers without a current bond, overdue RAAFs and CRAAFs, the integrity of the sealed log, bank accounts not yet reconciled, funds without a bank account, revenue targets not yet set, and the age of the latest encrypted backup. The treasurer then rates the office from 1 to 4 with a note. Ratings are kept per quarter, the two weakest principles are named, and the whole assessment prints as a signed report.

The principles are cumulative. Legality without documents cannot be proved. Documents without owners cannot be enforced. Owners without deadlines can delay forever. Deadlines without seals produce reports no one can trust. And all of it fails if it ends when the builder leaves. That is the full circle: 360°.

title: A Research Agenda and Questions for Practitioners

r: The ALTOS principles are a practitioner’s theory, and they should now be tested. This chapter proposes research questions for graduate students and scholars of public administration, and reflection questions for treasury officers.

head: Area
Question
Possible method
rows: Does automated, rule-enforcing collection raise own-source revenue in lower-income (fourth- and fifth-class) municipalities?

Interrupted time series on submission dates

r: For each principle of Chapter 14, a treasurer may ask:

items: Can I name the law or ordinance behind every account on our receipts?
Is there any peso we receive or release without a form?
Is every accountable officer bonded today, for the right amount?
Which report is due next, and who is likely to be late?
If someone changed a posted record last night, how would I know?
Where in my office does one person act alone, and what compensates for it?
Is every fund kept in its own account and shown separately in our reports?
What would a farmer from our farthest barangay say about paying taxes here?
What did the figures tell me this month, and what did I decide because of them?

blocks.text: 15.3 Toward a Philippine theory of public fiscal administration

r: Philippine public administration has long adapted imported theory to local conditions: diverse communities, limited resources, a strong tradition of local autonomy and a resilient civil service. Public fiscal administration is a promising place to build theory from below, because its records are rich, its rules are explicit and its results are measurable. Every local treasury is a laboratory. The founders of public administration studied their own governments. Filipino practitioners and scholars can do the same with theirs.
